reason: Declining (declinate) stems, branches, spines and fruits are directed or curved obliquely downward, which is FLOPO descending. Prostrate stems that rise at the tip would be PATO_0002343 decumbent, but these examples do not say that.
A degree word ('little branched', 'little or no blade'). It modifies another value and is not a quality itself.

target: new: apex of the bearer (plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023, part-of-bearer slot) + orange (PATO_0000953)
reason: The colour belongs to the tip, not the whole corolla, petal or hair. This is the same apex reading as the 'gland-tipped' rule, with orange as the quality.

target: new: coloured marking of the bearer (streaked FLOPO:0991206, marking colour red PATO_0000322)
reason: Two values run together: the bearer has thin lines of another colour (streaked), and those lines are red. Red applies to the marks, not the whole petal.
A surface of close-set pits separated by a raised network is what the alveolate definition already describes (honeycomb-like). 'Reticulate' only names the walls between the pits.
'Turned' carries no direction of its own ('upward', 'downward', 'to one side'). The direction is the quality, and it is read from the phrase around it.
A weakly defined petiole, vein or region is one that is not clearly visible. This follows the earlier rules that mapped 'obscure' and 'indistinct' to inconspicuous.
This is a heading, not a quality: the shape word that follows (rounded, cuneate, cordate) applies to the base of the part, as in the earlier 'base' rule.
A comparison stated without the part it is compared with, like the earlier rejections of 'darker' and 'narrower'.
Teeth or segments pointing forward, toward the apex, are antrorse: curved forward or upward.
An excised apex or base has a notch cut into it, and PATO emarginate means a notched tip or edge.
Honeycomb-like fruit surfaces are alveolate by definition. Honeycomb-like veins are better read as FLOPO:0991100 reticulate if the bearer is a vein.
Densely packed spikelets, glomerules and inflorescences are crowded: set close together.

target: new: two values of one bearer (pinnately veined FLOPO:0991201 and reticulate FLOPO:0991100)
reason: Both values hold together: pinnate main veins joined by a network of finer veins. This is not a point between two shapes.

target: new: coloured marking of the bearer (streaked FLOPO:0991206, marking colour red PATO_0000322)
reason: Same as red-lined: the bearer is streaked, and the streaks are red.
A running rhizome or rootstock is a long creeping one. 'Veins running to the margin' is a relation to another part and is not covered by this rule.
A tattered ligule apex or leaf tip has an irregular, torn-looking edge, which is lacerate.
The definition of virgate covers branching systems with long, slender, erect, wand-like axes.
Like the earlier rejection of 'covered': the quality is the coating (sand, wax, bloom), which the word does not name.
A count of spikelets (PO_0009051) with the vague number 'few', handled like 'few-flowered'. This needs the suffix 'spiculate' -> spikelet added to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.

target: pseudostipule (no PO class; a FLOPO anatomy class is needed) present
reason: This states that pseudostipules (stipule-like outgrowths at the leaf base) are present. It is not stipulate, and PO has no pseudostipule class, so the rule waits on a FLOPO part class.
In pollen and spore descriptions, psilate means a smooth wall with no sculpturing.

label: sweet-tasting
definition: A flavourful quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a sweet taste, like sugar. NOTE: Taste counterpart of FLOPO:0991016 sweet-scented; PATO has no named tastes below flavourful.
reason: Fruit and aril taste is a real diagnostic character, and PATO has no term for sweet taste. 'Sour-tasting' would be a sibling class.
A tail-like apex, point or appendage means the bearer is caudate: having a tail-like projection.
A count of 3 longitudinal grooves: sulcate (FLOPO:0991061) with the count held in the count pattern, not a new term.
A misspelling of acuminate.

label: catenate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of structures of the same kind by virtue of their being joined end to end in a series, like the links of a chain. NOTE: Not FLOPO:0991168 moniliform, which is a single structure constricted at intervals.
reason: Tubers and pseudobulbs joined in a chain are an arrangement of several like parts. No PATO or FLOPO term covers this, and moniliform is the shape of a single part.
An adverb that grades the following value ('coarsely serrate'). It is a value qualifier, not a quality on its own.
Lozenge-shaped means rhombic, which the earlier rules for 'rhombic' and 'rhomboidal' mapped to PATO rhomboid.
This negates 'broadened' or 'expanded', which the earlier rule mapped to PATO dilated.
